blocks.text: The VSEPR model predicts and explains the shapes of molecules but gives no reason for the formation of bonds. Valence bond theory is concerned with both the formation of bonds and the shapes of molecules. This way of describing a covalent bond treats a molecule as a combination of atoms.

items: A covalent bond is formed when half-filled orbitals in the valence shells of two atoms of similar energy overlap.
A greater overlap of the orbitals results in a stronger bond.
Covalent bonds are directional: the direction of the bond is determined by the shape and mode of the overlapping orbitals.

blocks.prompt: What does VBT add to VSEPR, and what must be true of two orbitals before they can form a bond?
blocks.explanation: VSEPR only predicts shapes; VBT explains why bonds form as well as the shapes. For a bond, each atom must bring a half-filled valence orbital, the two orbitals must be of similar energy, and they must overlap; the more they overlap the stronger the bond, and the direction of overlap fixes the bond's direction.

items: VBT explains both bond formation and shape: a covalent bond is the overlap of half-filled valence orbitals of similar energy; more overlap means a stronger bond; bonds are directional.
